summary: Feed s100_single to NDR is degraded: 17.1% of frames are truncated/sliced to ~128 bytes (418/2442), exceeding 5% threshold. NDR requires full payload for detection. All other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, VLAN, drops, overload, encryption, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is configured with packet slicing / snaplen truncation at 128 bytes, cutting payload before delivery to tool port. Most truncated frames are exactly 128 bytes, classic broker slicing behavior to save bandwidth.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection, signature matching, and anomaly detection. With 17.1% of frames cut short, payload-dependent detections, file extraction, and IDS signatures will miss or misclassify attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing/snaplen on the broker policy for s100_single and forward full frames up to the NDR's 9216 byte MTU so the NDR receives complete L4+ payload for analysis.
